# Drainage-tree measures (generated by scripts/probes/treeTable.py)

Columns: mtn% = mountain share of land; dist p90/p99 = mountain cells' distance to the front, km; conf45/conf200 = confluences whose two branches both drain >= 45 / 200 km² (inside% = on mountain ground or upstream of a range exit, plain% = on plain ground); exitsT = range exits draining >= T km² (NN = nearest-neighbour spacing p25/p50/p75, km; A = catchment, km²); top3% = share of all water crossing the front carried by the three largest exits; exit/mouth = for rivers reaching the sea with >= 500 km² fed from the ranges, the largest single exit's catchment over the mouth's (p25/p50/p75); exits/river = exits >= 10 km² feeding such a river (p50); Hack h over cells >= 10 km² (1 km lattice; router-dependent, see PLAN.md); Re = Schumm elongation (p50) of sea basins >= 100 km² and of range-exit basins >= 100 km². Classes: field = the generator's own fields (mountain: uplift >= 0.25 in ranges >= 100 km²; hill: hill amplitude >= 300 m); relief = max-min within 2 cells (5 km window) >= 500 m mountain, >= 150 m hill; uplift = the spike variant's own uplift >= 0.3 of peak. Drawn-network rows use the drawn lines (river heads at 45 km², so exits10 = exits45 for kind 0).
